method: fluidpy.diag.fronts.front_lines(T850, u, v, lat, lon, locate='centre') (Hewson 1998 TFP, 100-km smoothing, threshold 1.5 K/100 km); shown: the longest warm line within 400 km of the low and east of it, and the longest cold line (≥ 1000 km) within 900 km of the low and south of it
hourly_method: front_lines(T850, u, v, locate='centre') each hour, chosen by shape (fix loop 2, review 2 N-M2): warm = line E-SE of the tracked Ciarán centre (≤ 350 km, ≥ 300 km long, clipped to 800 km); cold = ≥ 800-km line trailing S-SW (≤ 500 km, not clipped); continuity = mean gap + 10 km/° orientation change; drawn while both exist from 12 UTC 1 Nov (to 21 UTC), then faded; after 21 UTC the trailing front has broken off the low and the only S-SW cold line lies 92-290 km SE of Brest before the station's 00-03 UTC cold-front passage, so the map shows no fronts after 21 UTC
